findings.title: Update invalidation uses organization-aware model and can miss login-cache invalidation
findings.body: In update(), the original model is fetched via getById(), which wraps the IDP so isEnabled() also requires the linked organization to be enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then uses this wrapped model in getLoginPredicate(). If the organization is disabled, the original predicate evaluates to false even when the IDP itself is enabled/public. An update that changes hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or brokerPublic to another non-login state can then satisfy !P(original) && !P(updated) and skip invalidation. The login cache may keep the IDP, and when the organization is re-enabled getForLogin can return a hidden, link-only, or non-public organization broker. Use the raw delegate model for the original state or compare the login-relevant fields directly instead of relying on the organization-aware predicate result.

findings.title: Cached getForLogin results are returned without re-validating login predicate
findings.body: getForLogin() caches only internal IDP IDs and, when serving from cache, loads each IDP and returns it without re-applying LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() or checking that the model is still enabled, not hidden, not link-only, and public if organization-linked. Organization state changes do not invalidate this cache, and the update invalidation logic can miss changes while an organization is disabled. As a result, the method can return IDPs that no longer satisfy the SPI contract for login-suitable providers. The changed login-page caller only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin/linkOnly/brokerPublic, so stale entries can still be exposed.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes literal "alias" instead of created identity provider aliases
findings.body: The cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal string "alias" instead of the variable alias used when creating the provider. The same mistake appears in testCacheIDPForLogin at lines 381 and 425 for the created idp-alias-* providers. Consequently the test does not remove the identity providers it creates, leaking realm state and potentially making other tests or assertions flaky.
